newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Falconbridge joins Konkola Deep consortium.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge joins Konkola Deep consortium.

text.p: Canada's Falconbridge Ltd has joined a South Africa-led consortium to develop Zambia's Konkola Deep copper mine, Anglo American Corporation of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday.
"Anglo can confirm that Falconbridge is the third partner in the consortium," an Anglo spokeswoman told Reuters.

The Zambia Privatisation Agency said in October that a Canadian company -- which it declined to name -- had expressed interest in joining the consortium negotiating with the Zambian government to develop the Konkola Deep mine.
Falconbridge last year had a turnover of C$2.3 billion and sold some 159,000 tonnes of copper and 91,000 tonnes of nickel.

Zambia sees the US$600 million development of the Konkola Deep mine as crucial to the country's mining industry which has been hard hit by declining copper output and depressed prices on the world market.

The Zambian government and the consortium, led by Anglo's Bermuda-based unit Zambia Copper Investments Ltd (ZCI), signed a formal letter of understanding in January this year on the development of the mine.

The development would be done in conjunction with state-run Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM), which has been offered for sale by the Lusaka government as part of its drive to privatise state assets.
South Africa's Gencor Ltd is the other consortium partner.
Australian-based Western Mining Corp (WMC) pulled out of the consortium in July.

ZCI said recently that subject to a satisfactory outcome to the negotiations with the Zambian government, the consortium and the government were committed to "implementation of the project at the earliest possible date".
Anglo said discussion with the Zambian government was still continuing.

"We are still in discussions with the Zambian government. There are no new developments. At such stage as the memorandum of agreement is signed, then the nature of the consortium will be of significance," the Anglo spokeswoman said.
The indentified ore resource at the Konkola Deep mine contains 340 million tonnes at 3.8 percent copper content.
The project envisages mining the ore body to a depth of around 1,740 metres to produce around six million tonnes of ore a year.
Planned output would be around 180,000 tonnes of finished copper a year.
Zambia produced around 380,000 tonnes of copper last year, making it the world's seventh largest producer.
